page: Amazon Web Services i8g.large is an arm64 storage-optimized instance powered by AWS Graviton processors with custom Neoverse-V2 cores clocked at 2.8 GHz. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture, this instance allocates two dedicated physical cores with a single thread per core, paired with 16.0 GB of memory for an 8.0 GB per core ratio. Cache levels feature 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 36 MB L3 cache. In addition to hardware-accelerated AES encryption instructions, it bundles a 468 GB local NVMe SSD and provides a baseline network throughput of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results demonstrate dependable single-core performance alongside typical entry-tier multi-core limits. The instance recorded average tier marks on Geekbench single-core (1813.0) and stress-ng single-core (1707.28), with single-threaded bzip3 decompression ranking in the top 25% at 14.15 GB/sec. Conversely, total compute throughput is bounded by its 2-vCPU configuration, landing multi-core stress-ng (3402.28) and Geekbench multi-core (3235.0) in lower tiers. Memory tests show balanced uncached read bandwidth at 56.64 GB/sec and average PassMark database operation scores of 3025.4.

From an architectural standpoint, the combination of energy-efficient Graviton silicon, direct NVMe scratch capacity, and high per-core RAM offers qualitative cost efficiency for I/O-sensitive workloads that do not require massive parallel compute. The primary tradeoffs lie in entry-level baseline networking of 1 Gbps and modest multi-threaded compute density, making it best suited for lightweight relational databases, transactional key-value stores, local caching nodes, and disk-intensive data processing pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services i8g.large is a storage-optimized virtual machine featuring two dedicated arm64 AWS Graviton Neoverse-V2 cores operating at 2.8 GHz on the Nitro hypervisor. The instance includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 8.0 GB per core, and bundles a dedicated 468 GB NVMe SSD alongside a 1 Gbps baseline network link. Synthetic testing displays competent single-threaded execution, highlighted by strong bzip3 decompression speeds and average Geekbench single-core metrics, balanced against lower multi-threaded throughput expected from a 2-vCPU envelope. Database operations and uncached memory reads achieve consistent middle-tier benchmark results. With its lean CPU footprint, generous memory allocation, and direct-attached NVMe storage, i8g.large is functionally configured for localized transactional databases, caching layers, and storage-heavy edge workloads.
